title: Local capacity, population change, belonging, trust, and civic action do not form a single place gradient
source_unit: Deliberately non-pooled county-context respondent cells, local-area attitude samples, and national respondent cross-tabs
geography: United States; county contexts nationally and Chicago, suburban Cook County, and Lake County, Illinois

observations.period: 2024; CES respondents grouped by county population change, 2020-2023

denominator.unit: valid CES respondents across four population-change groups; 155 represented counties in the place frame

federal_trust.unit: percent trusting federal government a great deal or fair amount

civic_action.unit: percent reporting at least one selected civic action

state_trust.unit: percent trusting state government a great deal or fair amount

observations.method: Weighted descriptive CES common-content comparison using commonpostweight; counties with at least 100,000 residents and valid 2020/2023 population estimates were split into four place-count quartiles.
observations.uncertainty: No complex-survey standard errors or county-representative estimates were computed; county FIPS supplies context but respondents are not a county probability sample. Population change includes births, deaths, domestic migration, and international migration.
observations.subgroup: CES respondents linked to counties in the four population-change context groups; respondent denominators and represented counties differ by group.
observations.counterinterpretation: The relatively stable civic-action shares and non-monotonic trust pattern do not show that growth or decline caused political meaning; party identity, composition, selection, and local conditions remain unmeasured.

denominator.unit: valid CES respondents across four health-establishment-density × zero-vehicle-share cells; counties >=100,000 population

federal_trust.unit: percent trusting federal government a great deal or fair amount across cells

state_trust.unit: percent trusting state government a great deal or fair amount across cells

civic_action.unit: percent reporting at least one selected civic action across cells

population_change_median.unit: median county population change, 2020-2023, within cells

observations.method: Weighted descriptive CES common-content comparison after county-keyed assignment to CBP health/social-assistance establishment density and ACS zero-vehicle-household-share cells, split at unweighted county medians.
observations.uncertainty: No complex-survey standard errors or county-representative estimates; the cell measures county context, not respondent-level service exposure, provider use, transport reliability, or access quality. ACS margins of error are not propagated.
observations.subgroup: CES respondents in four county context cells defined by health-establishment capacity and zero-vehicle share; cell counts and represented counties differ.
observations.counterinterpretation: A high zero-vehicle share may reflect transit, density, disability, poverty, or settlement structure; health-establishment density is not provider adequacy, affordability, or realized care. Trust/action variation is not a causal capacity effect.

observations.period: April 13-23, 2026; local immigration meaning and legal-inclusion attitudes

denominator.unit: unweighted adults across Chicago (758), suburban Cook County (742), and Lake County (400); item-specific valid samples

favor_citizenship_path.unit: weighted percent favoring a citizenship path for undocumented immigrants

favor_dreamer_status.unit: weighted percent favoring permanent legal status for Dreamers

observations.method: Weighted mixed-mode local survey with reported adjustment for gender, age, race/ethnicity, education, PUMA, and 2024 presidential vote; reported margins of error are +/-3.6 points for Chicago and suburban Cook and +/-4.9 for Lake County.
observations.uncertainty: These are local attitude estimates, not county-wide causal estimates or measures of service use, migration flows, labor outcomes, or political action. Question wording, nonresponse, mode, and subgroup limits remain.
observations.subgroup: Adults surveyed in English or Spanish in three Illinois areas; each geography has a separate denominator and margin of error.
observations.counterinterpretation: Broad support for Dreamer status can coexist with conditional views on immigration levels, border policy, admission rules, local services, and fiscal allocation; local attitude differences do not identify the material cause.

observations.period: 2024; national immigration meaning, trust, and vote cross-tabs

denominator.unit: maximum valid unweighted ANES 2024 post-election cross-tab cases; item-specific denominators range from 3654 to 4882

economic_meaning_and_decrease_a_lot.unit: row percent among respondents saying immigration is extremely bad for the economy

job_competition_and_decrease_a_lot.unit: row percent among respondents saying job competition is extremely likely

citizenship_path_and_same_level.unit: row percent among respondents favoring a conditional citizenship path

trump_vote_and_decrease_a_lot.unit: row percent among valid reported Trump-vote respondents

observations.method: Official UC Berkeley SDA complex-design weighted row cross-tabs using ANES 2024 post-election weight V240107b and Taylor-series standard errors for selected cells.
observations.uncertainty: Economic meaning, perceived job competition, legal inclusion, desired level, trust, and reported vote are separate items; the cross-tabs are descriptive, not causal, and perceived exposure is not measured local labor-market exposure.
observations.subgroup: Rows defined by economic evaluation, perceived job competition, legal-inclusion view, or reported vote; valid cases differ by table.
observations.counterinterpretation: A respondent can favor legal inclusion while preferring no increase or a decrease in immigration, and party identity, ideology, information, race, religion, and candidate evaluation may structure all items.

related_sources.claim: CES county-linked growth and capacity/trust/action context files.

boundary: This is a non-pooled place-to-meaning comparison. It does not establish that growth, capacity, mobility, migration, or service access caused trust, belonging, immigration judgment, civic action, or vote. A same-geography panel linking dated exposure, material/service conditions, attribution, belonging, action, and institutional response remains open.
